February 6, 2011
Melissa Johnson
General Manager
Scott, Smith and Edwards
Dear Ms. Johnson:
Thank you for the time you and your colleagues have given us over recent weeks in
describing how Scott, Smith and Edwards runs today and what you would want a
reconsidered operating model to make possible. I am writing to record, as plainly as
I am able, the terms on which our firm would carry that work forward, so that once
you have read this letter and, if it sets out the understanding we reached, returned a
signed copy to me, there is a single document to which either of us may turn should
a question ever arise about what we agreed. I have tried throughout to describe only
what I am confident the firm can deliver, and if any passage here reads as promising
more than that, I would ask you to raise it with me before you sign.
The Work You Have Asked Us to Undertake
As I understand the assignment, Scott, Smith and Edwards has reached a point
where the way the business is organised to serve its customers, and in particular the
way its online channels sit alongside the rest of the operation, deserves a considered
examination from outside. You have asked us to look at the operating model as a
whole, at the roles and the responsibilities that compose it, at the processes that
connect them, and at the economics that sit beneath them, and to return to you with
a design you can act on. Our work will move from an orderly reading of how the
organisation operates today, through a view of where the digital channels genuinely
change what the work requires, to a set of recommendations on the structure, the
processes, and the investment that a revised model would call for. What the
engagement does not extend to is the running of your operation, which remains
entirely yours to direct, nor to legal, tax, or accounting advice, on which you should
continue to rely on the advisers who ordinarily provide it; where our analysis
touches those matters, what we offer is a reasoned business view and not a
professional opinion in their place.

How We Propose to Proceed
Our manner of working is deliberate, and I hope you will find it plain rather than
clever. We begin by listening, to you and to the people who already carry a working
view of how the day is actually run, and only then do we set down the small number
of judgments the operating model truly turns on and build the analysis outward from
them, so that every recommendation we eventually place before you can be traced
back to the evidence that supports it. Where that evidence will bear a firm
recommendation we will give you one, and where it will bear only a range or a
caution we will tell you that instead, because a recommendation that outruns what
we actually know is of no use to you and no credit to us.
The People on the Engagement
I will keep my own hand on the engagement and will read anything of consequence
before it leaves the firm under our name, but the daily work would sit with two of
our people whom I would ask you to come to know. Jason Torres, a Principal of the
firm, would lead the engagement and be your point of contact from the first meeting
through to the close; he is direct in the way that operators tend to prefer, and I
would encourage you to be as direct with him in return. Deborah Allen, a
Consultant, would carry the analysis and build the exhibits on which the
recommendations rest, and she keeps her work close to the evidence, so that a
question about any figure can be answered from its source rather than from
memory. You are welcome to reach me at any time, though for most day-to-day
matters Jason Torres will be the quicker route to an answer.
Fee and Start Date
Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is $106,000, which covers the
time of the people named above through the completion of the work, and against
which we will render invoices as the engagement proceeds. The work would begin
on February 16, 2011, and we would move into the first interviews and information
requests promptly thereafter, so that the early weeks are not lost to setting up what
could have been arranged in advance.
Fees and Payment
Each invoice we render against the fee stated above will be payable within thirty
days of your receipt of it. The fee covers our people and their time and not the
incidental costs of the assignment, such as travel or the reproduction of materials,
which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they
cost us and no more; and should the shape of the work change materially from what

this letter contemplates, I will raise the question of the fee with you and we will
settle it together before any further work is done, so that nothing ever reaches you
on an invoice as a surprise.
Term and Termination
We expect the engagement to run for something on the order of three months,
though I would ask you to treat that as an honest estimate of the work rather than a
promise about the calendar, since we will regard the assignment as complete when
it is genuinely done and not merely when a given number of weeks has passed.
Either of us may bring the engagement to an end on thirty days' written notice to
the other, and if you choose to do so you will owe us for the work properly
performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for
nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality
Everything we learn about Scott, Smith and Edwards in the course of this work we
will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of the engagement. That
obligation binds every member of the team, it survives the end of our work together,
and it covers the fact of our involvement as fully as it covers its substance. We would
ask the same of you in respect of the methods and the written materials we share
with you, which represent the firm's own way of working and are meant for your use
and not for wider circulation.
Limitation of Liability
We will perform the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm
engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the
commercial and operational decisions that Scott, Smith and Edwards will ultimately
take on the strength of our advice, nor the conditions in which those decisions play
out, and so, save to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to
you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law
This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established,
and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state.
Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder will
continue in force, unaffected by it.
If this letter reflects the understanding we reached, I would be grateful if you would
sign the enclosed copy where indicated below and return it to me, keeping the

second copy for your own file; once your signed copy is in my hands, Jason Torres
will write to you to fix the first meetings and the initial requests for information, so
that we can begin without delay.
Julie Ramsey
Managing Principal
Date: February 6, 2011
Melissa Johnson
General Manager, Scott, Smith and Edwards
Date: February 6, 2011
Calderwood Partners LLC
